items.statement: The overall mean EQ-VAS score was 79.39 and the mean EQ-5D-5L index score was approximately 0.91; older respondents had lower EQ-VAS scores, and males had higher index scores than females.

items.statement: WHOQOL-BREF mean domain scores ranged from 58.53 to 69.23. Higher education and income generally corresponded to better quality-of-life scores, and older respondents had lower overall quality of life and health satisfaction.

items.statement: The authors concluded that the EQ-5D-5L descriptive system and WHOQOL-BREF had high test-retest reliability, but EQ-VAS and EQ-5D-5L index scores had poor agreement in this general population.
source: Full article, Conclusion

items.statement: The authors stated that the norms can provide reference data for clinicians, researchers, public-health experts, epidemiologists, and health-care workers.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraph beginning “Estimation of EQ-5D-5L and WHOQOL-BREF norms”

items.statement: The authors attributed the low EQ-VAS and index-score ICCs partly to the highly skewed general-population EQ-5D-5L data and low variance, including a large proportion in health state 11111.

items.statement: The total sample mainly lived on Java, which raises uncertainty about representativeness for the whole Indonesian archipelago.
source: Full article, Discussion, limitations paragraph beginning “Several limitations”
